ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
During quarantine, the FBI has been monitoring a young physicists suspicious activities. After compiling weeks worth of evidence, the FBI finally has had enough and searches his room.

The room's door is opened with a high angular velocity about its hinge. Over a very short period of time, its angular velocity increases to $\omega=8.56 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ due to the force applied at the end opposite from the hinge. For simplicity, treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length $L=1.00 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $M=9.50 \mathrm{~kg}$. The hinge (pivot) is located at one end of the rod. Ignore gravity. At what distance from the hinge of the door is the door most likely to break? Assume that the door will break at where the bending moment is largest. (Answer in metres.)

A distance x is marked from the hinge to a trial cut point, an angular velocity ω is indicated about the hinge, and an upward force F is applied at the far right end. The internal bending moment at the cut balances the moment from the applied tip force minus the moment from the distributed tangential inertial force. During quarantine, the FBI has been monitoring a young physicist's suspicious activities. After compiling weeks worth of evidence, the FBI finally has had enough and searches his room.

The room's door is opened with a high angular velocity about its hinge. Over a very short period of time, its angular velocity increases to $\omega = 8.56\ \mathrm{rad/s}$ due to the force applied at the end opposite from the hinge. For simplicity, treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length $L = 1.00\ \mathrm{m}$ and mass $M = 9.50\ \mathrm{kg}$. The hinge (pivot) is located at one end of the rod. Ignore gravity. At what distance from the hinge of the door is the door most likely to break? Assume that the door will break where the bending moment is largest. (Answer in metres.)

method.method_draft: Use a free-body diagram of the portion of the rod to the right of a trial break point x. Read the rod as hinged at the left with an upward force F applied at the right end. Let linear density be λ = M/L and angular acceleration be α. The end force and angular acceleration are related by the whole-rod torque equation FL = Iα = (1/3)ML^2α, so F = λαL^2/3. For the segment from x to L, the internal bending moment at the cut balances the moment of the tip force F(L - x) minus the moment of the distributed tangential inertial force λ α r over x ≤ r ≤ L: M_b(x) = F(L - x) - ∫_x^L λ α r(r - x) dr. Centripetal acceleration is along the rod and gives no bending moment. Substitute F = λαL^2/3 to get M_b(x) = (λα/6)x(L^2 - x^2). Maximize by setting dM_b/dx = (λα/6)(L^2 - 3x^2) = 0, giving x = L/√3 = √3/3 m for L = 1.00 m.

Image description: The figure shows a horizontal rod representing the door, hinged at the left end. A distance x is marked from the hinge to a trial cut point, an angular velocity ω is indicated about the hinge, and an upward force F is applied at the far right end.

Reasoning: Treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length L and mass M, with linear density λ = M/L. Let the angular acceleration during the short forcing interval be α. For the whole rod about the hinge, the applied end force satisfies FL = Iα. Since I = (1/3)ML^2 for a uniform rod about one end, FL = (1/3)ML^2α, so F = (1/3)MLα = λαL^2/3.

Now consider the segment of the rod to the right of a trial break point x. The internal bending moment at the cut balances the moment from the applied tip force minus the moment from the distributed tangential inertial force. The centripetal acceleration is along the rod, so it does not contribute to bending. Thus
M_b(x) = F(L - x) - ∫_x^L λα r(r - x) dr.
Substituting F = λαL^2/3 gives
M_b(x) = (λα/6)x(L^2 - x^2).
To find where the bending moment is largest, differentiate:
dM_b/dx = (λα/6)(L^2 - 3x^2).
Set this equal to zero:
L^2 - 3x^2 = 0, so x = L/√3.
With L = 1.00 m, x = 1/√3 = √3/3 m ≈ 0.577 m.

method.method_draft: Model the rotating door as a beam with a spatially varying transverse inertial load. From the geometry, take coordinate r from the hinge to the free end. The transverse distributed load due to angular acceleration is q(r) = λ α r, while the centripetal term is axial and does not enter the bending equation. The internal bending moment B(r) satisfies the beam relation B''(r) = -q(r) = -λ α r. At the free end, B(L) = 0, and the shear/bending-slope boundary is B'(L) = -F. Relate the applied end force to angular acceleration using FL = (1/3)ML^2α, hence F = λαL^2/3. Integrating B'' = -λ α r with these boundary conditions gives B(r) = (λα/6)r(L^2 - r^2). The maximum occurs where B'(r) = (λα/6)(L^2 - 3r^2) = 0, so r = L/√3. With L = 1.00 m, the distance is √3/3 m.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中把门简化成一根水平细杆，左端是铰链/转轴，门绕左端以角速度方向标记为 \(\omega\) 转动；右端受到垂直于杆的外力 \(F\)。距离变量从铰链沿杆向右量取，图中也标出了类似 \(x\) 的距离。推理：令从铰链到自由端的坐标为 \(r\)，杆长为 \(L\)，线密度为 \(\lambda=M/L\)。门的角加速度为 \(\alpha\) 时，横向惯性分布载荷为 \(q(r)=\lambda \alpha r\)。向心项沿杆方向，是轴向效应，不进入弯曲方程。内弯矩 \(B(r)\) 满足 \(B''(r)=-q(r)=-\lambda\alpha r\)。自由端边界条件为 \(B(L)=0\)，并且剪力边界为 \(B'(L)=-F\)。外力矩给出 \(FL=I\alpha=(1/3)ML^2\alpha\)，所以 \(F=\lambda\alpha L^2/3\)。积分得 \(B'(r)=-\lambda\alpha r^2/2+C_1\)。由 \(B'(L)=-\lambda\alpha L^2/3\)，得到 \(C_1=\lambda\alpha L^2/6\)。再积分并用 \(B(L)=0\)，得到 \(B(r)=(\lambda\alpha/6)r(L^2-r^2)\)。最大弯矩位置满足 \(B'(r)=(\lambda\alpha/6)(L^2-3r^2)=0\)，因此 \(r=L/\sqrt{3}\)。给定 \(L=1.00\,\mathrm{m}\)，距离为 \(1/\sqrt{3}=\sqrt{3}/3\,\mathrm{m}\)，约为 \(0.577\,\mathrm{m}\)。

During quarantine, the FBI has been monitoring a young physicist's suspicious activities. After compiling weeks worth of evidence, the FBI finally has had enough and searches his room.

The room's door is opened with a high angular velocity about its hinge. Over a very short period of time, its angular velocity increases to $\omega = 8.56\ \mathrm{rad/s}$ due to the force applied at the end opposite from the hinge. For simplicity, treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length $L = 1.00\ \mathrm{m}$ and mass $M = 9.50\ \mathrm{kg}$. The hinge (pivot) is located at one end of the rod. Ignore gravity. At what distance from the hinge of the door is the door most likely to break? Assume that the door will break where the bending moment is largest. (Answer in metres.)

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows a horizontal rod representing the door, hinged at the left end. A distance x is marked from the hinge to a trial cut point, an angular velocity ω is indicated about the hinge, and an upward force F is applied at the far right end.

Reasoning: Treat the door as a uniform thin rod of length L and mass M, with linear density λ = M/L. Let the angular acceleration during the short forcing interval be α. For the whole rod about the hinge, the applied end force satisfies FL = Iα. Since I = (1/3)ML^2 for a uniform rod about one end, FL = (1/3)ML^2α, so F = (1/3)MLα = λαL^2/3.

Now consider the segment of the rod to the right of a trial break point x. The internal bending moment at the cut balances the moment from the applied tip force minus the moment from the distributed tangential inertial force. The centripetal acceleration is along the rod, so it does not contribute to bending. Thus
M_b(x) = F(L - x) - ∫_x^L λα r(r - x) dr.
Substituting F = λαL^2/3 gives
M_b(x) = (λα/6)x(L^2 - x^2).
To find where the bending moment is largest, differentiate:
dM_b/dx = (λα/6)(L^2 - 3x^2).
Set this equal to zero:
L^2 - 3x^2 = 0, so x = L/√3.
With L = 1.00 m, x = 1/√3 = √3/3 m ≈ 0.577 m.
